answer_text:
Let \(\Phi\) be a bounded linear functional on \(\ell^2\). By the Riesz representation theorem, there exists a sequence \(a=(a_n)\in \ell^2\) such that

\[
\Phi(x)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty x_n \overline{a_n}, \qquad x\in \ell^2.
\]

Taking \(x=e_n=(0,\dots,0,1,0,\dots)\), we get

\[
b_n=\Phi(e_n)=\overline{a_n}.
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty |b_n|^2=\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|^2<\infty.
\]

So \((b_n)\in \ell^2\).

Now if \(p\ge 2\), since \(b_n\to 0\), for all sufficiently large \(n\) we have \(|b_n|\le 1\), and therefore

\[
|b_n|^p\le |b_n|^2.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty |b_n|^p<\infty \qquad \text{for every } p\ge 2.
\]

So \(p=2\) always works.

It remains to check that no smaller \(p\ge 1\) works in general. Let \(1\le p<2\) and choose

\[
a_n=n^{-1/p}.
\]

Then

\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|^2
=
\sum_{n=1}^\infty n^{-2/p}<\infty
\]

because \(2/p>1\). So \(a\in \ell^2\), and it defines a bounded linear functional \(\Phi\). But

\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|^p
=
\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac1n=\infty.
\]

Thus for every \(p<2\), there is a bounded linear functional on \(\ell^2\) for which \(\sum |b_n|^p\) diverges.

Therefore the optimal, smallest universal exponent is

\[
\boxed{2}.
\]
